standard_text: 8.8A write one-variable equations or inequalities with variables on both sides that represent problems using rational number coefficients and constants; 8.8B write a corresponding real-world problem when given a one-variable equation or inequality with variables on both sides of the equal sign using rational number coefficients and constants; 8.8C model and solve one-variable equations with variables on both sides of the equal sign that represent mathematical and real-world problems using rational number coefficients and constants

key_big: Move the variable terms to one side, then solve.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Get the variable terms on one side: subtract the smaller variable term from both sides.
  • Then undo the constants and divide.
  • Distribute and combine like terms first if there are parentheses.
  • If the variables cancel: a true statement (5 = 5) means infinitely many solutions; a false one (3 = 7) means no solution.

Examples

Example

5x + 3 = 2x + 15

Subtract 2x: 3x + 3 = 15

3x = 12

Answer: x = 4

Example

Gym A: 30 + 5v. Gym B: 10 + 9v.

30 + 5v = 10 + 9v

20 = 4v

Answer: v = 5 visits

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding the variable termsSubtract 2x from both sides, do not add it.
Distributing to only the first term3(x + 2) = 3x + 6.
Stopping at 0 = 00 = 0 means every number is a solution.

items.e: Both sides are exactly the same, so every number works. Infinitely many solutions.
Subtract 2x from both sides: 7 = −1. That is never true, so there is no solution.

items.q: Which right side makes 4x + 7 = ? have no solution?
items.e: Use the same x-term but a different number: 4x + 7 = 4x + 10 is never true. The answer is 4x + 10.
Subtract 3x from both sides: 0 = 2. That is never true, so there is no solution.
2x + 8 = 3x + 8 gives x = 0. Zero is a solution: one solution.

items.q: Which right side makes 5x − 2 = ? have infinitely many solutions?
items.e: Make the right side exactly the same: 5x − 2.
The x-terms are different (8x and −8x), so you can solve: x = 0. One solution.

items.q: Which right side makes 3x + 9 = ? have one solution?
items.e: A different x-term gives exactly one solution. The answer is 5x + 9.
Subtract x from both sides: −9 = 9. That is never true, so there is no solution.
2x + 3 = 2x + 5 has the same x-term on both sides but different numbers, so it is never true. The answer is 2x + 3 = 2x + 5.
3x − 1 = 3x − 1 has the same expression on both sides, so every x works. The answer is 3x − 1 = 3x − 1.

items.q: Gym A charges $30 plus $5 per visit. Gym B charges $10 plus $9 per visit. For how many visits do they cost the same?
items.e: 30 + 5v = 10 + 9v, so 20 = 4v and v = 5 visits.

items.q: Jo has $45 and saves $6 a week. Max has $81 and saves $3 a week. After how many weeks will they have the same amount?
items.e: 45 + 6w = 81 + 3w, so 3w = 36 and w = 12 weeks.

items.q: A plant is 8 cm tall and grows 2 cm a week. Another is 20 cm tall and grows 0.5 cm a week. When are they the same height?
items.e: 8 + 2w = 20 + 0.5w, so 1.5w = 12 and w = 8 weeks.

items.q: Taxi A: $4 plus $2.50 per mile. Taxi B: $7 plus $2 per mile. For how many miles is the cost the same?
items.e: 4 + 2.5m = 7 + 2m, so 0.5m = 3 and m = 6 miles.
